subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what the city is actually doing — flows of power, water, traffic and people.

subsystems.name: Communications layer
subsystems.role: carries many small, frequent readings cheaply and reliably.
parts: private mesh for tunnels and basements

subsystems.name: Data platform
subsystems.role: turns a flood of raw readings into a shared, trustworthy picture.

subsystems.name: Analytics and control
subsystems.role: decides what to do with the measurements.

subsystems.name: Actuation layer
subsystems.role: the part that actually changes the physical city.

subsystems.name: Digital twin
subsystems.role: a 3D, updatable model of the city used to test changes before building them.

buildSteps.title: Map what already exists
buildSteps.detail: Inventory pipes, cables, roads and substations, and record who owns and operates each one — most cities fail here first.

buildSteps.title: Agree a data model and rules
buildSteps.detail: Decide common formats, update rates and privacy rules before buying hardware, so systems can talk to each other for decades.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the priority systems
buildSteps.detail: Fit meters, sensors and controllers where the money is largest: electricity distribution, water networks, arterial traffic.

buildSteps.title: Build the network
buildSteps.detail: Lay fibre where capacity is needed and low-power radio where only small readings travel; keep safety-critical control off the public internet.

buildSteps.title: Stand up the data platform
buildSteps.detail: Ingest, clean and time-stamp the data, and publish APIs so many teams and suppliers can build on it.

buildSteps.title: Add models and controls
buildSteps.detail: Forecast demand, detect leaks and faults, and use adaptive signal control and demand response where trials show a real benefit.

buildSteps.title: Build the digital twin
buildSteps.detail: A 3D model is kept current from sensor data and used to test a new tram line, district energy loop or flood defence before spending capital.

buildSteps.title: Fix the underlying infrastructure
buildSteps.detail: Retrofit insulation, pipes and substations so that the savings the software finds can actually be delivered.

buildSteps.title: Operate and upgrade
buildSteps.detail: Run it as permanent infrastructure with maintenance, spare parts and security patching, not a one-off project.

prerequisites.why: instrumenting a whole city is only affordable if each point costs little and runs for years on a battery.
they carry thousands of tiny messages per square kilometre without wiring every sensor.
centralised analytics works, but some control must happen locally to survive network outages.
without them each vendor's system is an island and integration costs swamp the savings.
connecting traffic, water and power controls to networks creates a target that cities have historically not defended well.
software can only shift demand or reroute flows if the pipes, cables and chargers are capable of being controlled.

pathway.milestone: widely deployed single-purpose systems: smart electricity meters, adaptive traffic signals, district heating controls
pathway.unlocks: real, measurable savings in one service at a time.

pathway.milestone: city-wide data platforms and working digital twins
pathway.unlocks: cross-service decisions, such as siting charging points using both grid and traffic data.

pathway.milestone: coordinated demand response across power, heat, water and transport
pathway.unlocks: cities that shave peak loads instead of building more capacity.

pathway.milestone: regionally and nationally linked city systems sharing energy and freight data
pathway.unlocks: resource management at a genuinely large scale — if standards, security and funding keep up.
